item.title: Gauge-Invariant Phase Mapping to Intensity Lobes of Structured Light via Closed-Loop Atomic Dark States
item.description: arXiv:2512.23642v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an analytical model showing how the gauge-invariant loop phase in a three-level closed-loop atomic system imprints as bright-dark lobes in Laguerre Gaussian probe beam intensity patterns. In the weak probe limit, the output intensity in such systems include Beer-Lambert absorption, a scattering term and loop phase dependent interference term with optical depth controlling visibility. These systems enable mapping of arbitrary phases via interference rotation and offer a platform to measure Berry phase. Berry phase emerge as a geometric holonomy acquired by the dark states during adiabatic traversal of LG phase defined in a toroidal parameter space. Manifesting as fringe shifts which are absent in open systems, experimental realization using cold atoms or solid state platforms appears feasible, positioning structured light in closed-loop systems as ideal testbeds for geometric phases in quantum optics.
item.dc:creator: Nayan Sharma, Ajay Tripathi

item.title: Gravitational wave detection via photon-graviton scattering and quantum interference
item.description: arXiv:2601.20553v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a fully quantum field-theoretic framework for gravitational wave (GW) detection, describing the interaction as inelastic photon-graviton scattering. We demonstrate that for \textit{a coherent graviton state}, this microscopic model explicitly reproduces the standard classical geometric-optics time delay, providing a rigorous consistency test of the correspondence limit. We propose a detection scheme based on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, where the GW-induced spectral shifts render entangled photon pairs distinguishable. This encodes the gravitational signal into the modulation of photon coincidence rates --- a quantum observable robust against laser intensity noise. Furthermore, we show that non-classical graviton states, such as squeezed states, induce unique decoherence signatures, establishing theoretical bounds on gravitational decoherence and defining the operational limits for probing the quantum nature of gravity.
item.dc:creator: K. Hari (IIT Bombay), S. Shankaranarayanan (IIT Bombay)

item.title: Decoherence-Induced Multiphoton Interference
item.description: arXiv:2604.05422v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Decoherence is usually deemed detrimental to quantum information processing. Its control and minimization require significant costs and operating overheads, constituting a major hurdle to the practical deployment of quantum technologies. Yet, quantum mechanics provides for counterintuitive, sometimes surprisingly useful, phenomena and effects associated with decoherence, leading to unusual practical utilities. Here we demonstrate such an example of fundamental interest and practical potential, where quantum interference is created among multiple photons through their dissipative coupling to a shared reservoir. On a thin-film lithium niobate chip, we dissipatively link two spontaneous parametric down-converters through a common, highly lossy channel to create phase-sensitive multiphoton states. Our results show that faithful correlations can be established among two, three, and four photons, and tuned by shifting the relative phase between the driving pumps for the converters. This experiment highlights an under-explored territory in quantum science and technology, where loss and decoherence serve as resources, rather than adversaries, for quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Du, Jiuyi Zhang, Daniel L\'opez Mart\'inez, Santosh Kumar, Misagh Izadi, Yuping Huang

item.title: Dynamic Behaviors of Materials Under Angle-Resolved Experiments: A Matrix Framework for Nonlinear Physics
item.description: arXiv:2604.13752v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Matter and external stimuli interact dynamically almost everywhere in nature. Under an applied field, a material seldom stays in the state in which it was characterized, and its properties change with time. Angle-resolved experiments are the standard way to resolve direction-dependent properties, however, current theoretical tools for data analysis are built for static states, leaving dynamic behaviors largely neglected. Here, we develop a generalized ``input-coefficient-output'' (ICO) approach that constructs spatial operation matrices and symmetry-reduced coefficient matrices across diverse physical systems, as we verify for nonlinear optics, elasticity, electrostriction and magnetostriction, and a Python program is released for convenient application. Using angle-resolved polarized second-harmonic generation (SHG) as an example, we focus on the dynamic modeling of material properties under angle-dependent stimuli, construct dynamic matrix equations that capture the time-dependent evolution of material responses, and propose three dynamic models and a point-to-point data fitting method. For the SHG experiments performed on $T_d-$WTe$_2$, the discrete dynamic model captures the asymmetric characteristics of the measured polar pattern with a significantly improved coefficient of determination ($R^2$ increasing from 0.567 to 0.773), whereas conventional static models are constrained to a symmetric curve. The evolution operator extracted from the dynamic model connects the macroscopic measurement to microscopic intermediate states during their interaction with stimuli. This work provides a practical matrix framework for dynamic modeling of material properties, paving the way for exploring complex nonlinear physics under realistic experimental conditions.
item.dc:creator: Hongjin Xiong, Zhonghui Xia, Xuan Ye, Teng Ma

item.title: Ultrastrong Coupling Signatures in Photon Statistics from Terahertz Higgs-Polaritons
item.description: arXiv:2604.15417v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ultrastrong coupling regime of cavity photons and quantum materials has emerged as a pathway to modify materials properties, however definitive signatures of ultrastrong coupling remain elusive. Focusing on the quantum photon statistics of light transmitted through a cavity-embedded superconductor, we show that a two-photon Higgs polariton at strong coupling realizes a photonic nonlinearity at the single terahertz photon level. We find that as light-matter coupling increases, the photon statistics show pronounced changes due to the formation of a hybrid photon-matter dark-cavity state with finite photon occupancy, producing testable signatures of ultrastrong coupling. We derive a non-Markovian input output relation and study the cavity-embedded superconductor 2H-NbSe2 as it approaches ultrastrong light-matter coupling. Our results reveal a diagnostic for ultrastrong coupling in the two-photon coincidence statistics that is absent in total counts.
item.dc:creator: Spenser Talkington, Benjamin Kass, Martin Claassen

item.title: Broadband characterization of polarization mode dispersion for quantum communication channels
item.description: arXiv:2607.03202v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a method for characterizing depolarization in fiber channels carrying broadband polarization-encoded optical signals. Wavelength-dependent polarization mode dispersion maps each input polarization to a trajectory on the Poincar\'e sphere; we show that the singular value decomposition of the band-averaged rotation matrix yields, in closed form, the optimal input states, the associated mutually unbiased measurement bases, and the resulting projection error probabilities. The three singular values provide a compact, bandwidth-dependent channel signature that distinguishes first- from higher-order dispersion, and yield the bandwidth at which the worst-case error probability reaches 3% as a practical filtering budget. We perform a second-order analysis of the band average that treats the two higher-order mechanisms: variation of the differential group delay at a fixed principal-state axis and wander of that axis with wavelength. We characterize 12 deployed fiber links in Masdar City and demonstrate mitigation by concatenating two channels through a single polarization controller, a step towards nonlocal compensation. The analysis is implemented in an openly available Python library for fiber-channel characterization.

item.title: Norm of resonance states in quantum scattering and electromagnetic systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.22052v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Resonance states spatially diverge and are thus not square integrable. Instead, their norm is defined by the biorthogonal scalar product of left and right states. We replace the corresponding volume integral over infinite space by a convenient boundary integral in piecewise-homogeneous systems and apply this procedure to diverse physical settings. For a quantum particle in any number of dimensions we treat hard-wall and piecewise-constant potentials. For electromagnetic systems with piecewise-homogeneous material properties, we consider three-dimensional and effectively two-dimensional cavities.
item.dc:creator: Florian Lorenz, Jan M\"oseritz-Schmidt, Roland Ketzmerick

item.title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31924v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models and spatial resolution. Here we demonstrate a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model that establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit. We discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from a pinned state directly at the channel-dielectric interface of an organic transistor, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics that contradict models based on substrate patterning. This non-destructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final configuration opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.
